I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy clay loam, good water retention, but needs irrigation when the summer rains come late. With my son working in the city, I manage most of the field work myself or with hired day labor at key times. I can't afford to experiment much. I need reliable yields to cover household costs.

**Wheat (winter crop, full 6 mu):**
I'll plant the whole 6 mu to wheat in mid-October as usual, right after I prepare the soil. I use an improved variety — Jimai 22 has worked well for me for years, the extension station recommended it and I've seen it hold up against the late spring frosts we sometimes get. I'll do rotary tillage after the maize stalks are chopped and incorporated. I'll apply base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer plus urea — then top-dress at jointing stage. I'll irrigate three times: wintering water in November, jointing in April, and heading in May. Two pesticide sprays — spring herbicide and a combined fungicide-insecticide at heading to fight powdery mildew and aphids. I should get around 480 jin per mu — that's normal for me.

**Maize (summer crop, full 6 mu):**
Right after wheat harvest in June, I'll plant maize directly into the stubble — no tillage. I've done no-till summer maize for several years now. It saves money and my back. I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the cooperative has that year. I apply most of the fertilizer as a side-dress at the jointing-tasseling stage when the plant needs it most. Summer rains help but I'll pump the well if we get a dry stretch at tasseling. Two pesticide applications — herbicide right after emergence, then spray for corn borer and aphids around silking.
